title: Focus is a Feature: Keyboard Accessibility
summary: This lesson covers the critical importance of focus states for keyboard accessibility, detailing how to style focus rings, manage tab order, and implement focus traps. It emphasizes that accessibility is a legal and functional requirement, not just a stylistic choice.

transcript.text: Press Tab. Where did the focus go?
Outline none is not a style choice. It's a lawsuit.
A ring needs two pixels, an offset, and contrast on every background. If you kill the default, ship a better one.
Mouse users never asked for a ring. Keyboard users can't work without one. :focus-visible tells them apart. Click, no ring. Tab, ring. Both sides win.
Focus follows the DOM, not your layout. Reorder columns with CSS and tab starts teleporting across the page. Visual order and DOM order have to match.
A modal opens. Focus must lock inside. Tab cycles through the dialogue and wraps around. Escape closes it and hands focus back to the button that opened it.
40 links stand between tab and your content. A skip link jumps past all of them in one press. Invisible until focused. First element on the page.
Focus is a feature. Follow for more UX engineering. Save this for your next accessibility pass.

on_screen_text: THE FOCUS RING: Don't kill the ring.
Kill it? Ship a better one.
:FOCUS-VISIBLE: Ring for those who need it.
TAB ORDER: Focus follows the DOM.
SKIP LINK: Jump the header in one press.
before_after: A checkout form with invisible focus states is transformed into one with clear, accessible focus rings; a dashboard with chaotic tab order is corrected to follow logical DOM flow.
